comment: Professor Diaz cares about all her students. Dances for Everybody was a more cultural/political class rather than an actual dance class. Her assignments were a little confusing at times, and the grading criteria was not always clear, but the work was manageable compared to other FYS classes. As long as she can tell you are trying, you will do well.

She is great! By far the easiest FYS at this school, TAKE THIS IF YOU ARE A FRESHMAN. She is so nice but can definitely waste your time with random readings. Not much actual dancing. you must go to a couple of outside events. If you can finesse your way around writing about art/dance, then you'll be set!

dances for everybody. got significantly harder grading as semester goes on but work was straight forward. the more you participate and "dance" the more she likes you. class has little to do w dance, more culturally focused. lots of group work. 3 hrs 1 per week made class drag, seemed better when I picked class but ended up hating that part of it.

Prof Diaz is kind & creates an atmosphere where you can be creative. Homework assignments are completion based, & most of your grade comes from in class participation. Some classes are more involved than others, but she just wants everyone to try their best in class. I enjoyed class, it was fun to try new things & be pushed out of my comfort zone.

Dr. Diaz is a fun prof to have. You have somatic and creative responses for hw, but as long as you care and describe what we did, you get a 100. The group project is the final and it is so easy. DO NOT do the homework reading, its useless. Lastly, you have a research paper, but also so easy. PLZ take if u want an A.

I took Dances for EveryBody with professor Diaz. The topic was HIV in Richmond for this semester. As long as you're comfortable with moving and using very odd "dance" methods you should be fine. I am not a dancer at all so that was okay. Grading wise she's really not hard as long as you care you're fine. She allowed for revisions.

The more you participate in professor Diaz's class, the better you will do. The written assignments are not hard but they are essential if you want to get a lot out of the class. Professor Diaz provides students with a lot of choice. For projects, she typically allows collaboration.

She is a fun and free spirit! Whether you've danced your entire life or never taken a class, you'll really enjoy her class. She will help you improve your skills no matter what your experience level. Great class for stress relief or if you want to fulfill your performance gen ed!
